thumb.trace: The broad thumb arises from the radial mass on image-right and crosses down-left through one interphalangeal bend to its nail-bearing pad pressing the pen grip.

index.trace: The upper-left long ray originates at the dorsal distal palm, bends around the left side of the pen and descends to its separate narrow nail-bearing tip against the grip.

middle.trace: The next ray curls behind the index/pen contact and foreground thumb, then emerges immediately beneath the pen as the leftmost of the three lower nail-bearing tips; its exposed continuation under the grip distinguishes it from the index.

ring.trace: The next lower ray has a separate proximal fold in the palm under the thumb, then curves forward to the broad central lower nail-bearing tip on the paper; the local thumb overlap hides only part of its proximal contour.

little.trace: The ulnar ray follows the rightmost underside of the hand and ends in the smaller nail-bearing tip to the right of the ring, with its own short curved chain resting near the paper.

hands.count_observation: Five unique terminal rays are traced: thumb and index on the grip, plus three separate lower curled fingers. The thin strip behind the index is part of the folded middle-finger contour rather than an additional independent digit.
hands.length_observation: The index and thumb are raised around the pen while middle/ring/little are flexed toward the paper. Following curved segments, the lower little is shorter than its neighbors and neither middle nor ring has an obvious overlong segment; their nail heights differ with flexion. Thumb length and width are plausible for the near radial view.
hands.joint_observation: The index emerges from the long-finger row and thumb from the radial side. Three lower fingers remain distinct into the palm despite short overlaps. Visible bends and nails follow their own chains without a branch or merged tip. The whole hand, wrist and a short forearm fit; only the more proximal forearm extends out at image-right.

sequence.observation: One actual panel with one right hand was inspected. All five digit identities are internally coherent in the final writing grip; the pen-adjustment transition is not illustrated and is not approved by this anatomy record.

limitations: Actual original image and, where necessary, enlarged detail inspected. Single-view visual anatomy assessment only: hidden bone geometry, exact centerline lengths and physical feasibility are not measured. This report does not approve action fidelity or motion between the illustrated panels.
